context_edits.purpose: H1 Base64Variants.encodeToText: the former encode loop (quotes, three-byte groups, escaped linefeed every maxLineLength>>2 complete groups), composed of packGroup and appendBase64Group
H2 ByteArrayBuilder.packGroup: packs 1-3 bytes as unsigned octets into a big-endian 24-bit group value
import for the new CharTypes helper
H3 CharTypes.appendBase64Group: appends the variant's chunk (3 bytes) or partial (1-2 bytes) characters for one group value

ownership_reason: ByteArrayBuilder.packGroup documents that it packs one to three bytes big-endian into the low 24 bits of an int, taking each byte as an unsigned octet (0 to 255), with bits 24 to 31 always zero, so that the result lies between 0 and 0xFFFFFF. Its loop ORs each byte into the accumulator as given (bits |= data[offset + i]), so a byte of 0x80 or more is sign-extended and sets every higher bit. For the trigger's final group (0xC3, 0xA9) it returns 0xFFFFA900 instead of 0x00C3A900, which violates both documented properties. CharTypes.appendBase64Group documents that its bits argument must be laid out as packGroup returns it (0 to 0xFFFFFF, first byte in bits 16 to 23); it only forwards the value to the unchanged upstream Base64Variant.encodeBase64Chunk / encodeBase64Partial. Given a valid group value, including values with bit 23 set, it appends the right characters, as the new passing test TestBase64Codec::testCharactersPerGroup pins. Base64Variants.encodeToText documents only that it obtains each group value from packGroup and hands it, with the byte count, to appendBase64Group, plus the quotes and the escaped-linefeed counter. The existing passing test TestBase64Generation::testStreamingWrites pins that behaviour, because it compares the output with the independent generator encoders for four variants. Base64Variant.encode is a single delegation to encodeToText. The sign extension of the second byte overwrites the first byte's position inside the low 24 bits, so no mask at the caller or in appendBase64Group can recover it; both declared compensating edits leave the trigger at Y2Fm/6k=. Restoring the & 0xFF in packGroup alone makes the trigger and the full suite pass.

compensating.old: CharTypes.appendBase64Group(variant, sb, ByteArrayBuilder.packGroup(input, inputPtr, count), count);
compensating.new: CharTypes.appendBase64Group(variant, sb, ByteArrayBuilder.packGroup(input, inputPtr, count) & 0xFFFFFF, count);
